# The required angular surplus for saturated positive coefficients

Let d>=3 and let a_0,...,a_d be in [-1,1], with a_0=-1 and sum a_i=0.
Suppose every strictly positive coefficient equals one. For independent
unit exponentials E_i, put P=Pr(sum a_i E_i>=0). Then

    P>(7/6)(d/(d+1))^d.                                    (1)

This theorem retains the coefficient restriction. The general fractional-
positive stationary family is not disposed of by this note.

Let k be the number of positive coefficients and q=d-k. If k=1,
all remaining coefficients apart from a_0 are zero by the balance
constraint, and P=1/2. Since gamma_d decreases and
(7/6)gamma_3=63/128<1/2, (1) follows in this case.

For k>=2 the remaining q negative magnitudes, including possible zeros,
lie in [0,1] and sum to k-1. Thus q>=k-1 and
k<=floor((d+1)/2). The proved geometric-mode comparison gives

    P>=P_(k,q):=Pr(Gamma(k)>=Exp(1)+((k-1)/q)Gamma(q))
      >=G_k>9/20.

The last strict inequality is the proved all-k theorem
`candidate 49f9fad7c4bf7e35`.
For d>=10, monotonicity of gamma_d and the exact identity

    9/20-(7/6)(10/11)^10=310464227/1556245476060>0

prove (1). Monotonicity follows directly by differentiating
x log(x/(x+1)): its derivative is
-log(1+1/x)+1/(x+1)<0, since log(1+t)>t/(1+t) for t>0.

Here is a complete finite rational comparison for d=3,...,9. Tilting
Y=Exp(1)+((k-1)/q)Gamma(q) by e^(-Y) and expanding its integer moments
gives the exact expression

    P_(k,q)=(1/2)(q/(q+k-1))^q
       sum_(l=0)^(k-1) sum_(j=0)^l
          binom(q+j-1,j)((k-1)/(q+k-1))^j 2^(-(l-j)).         (2)

To see this without a distributional approximation, the gamma survival
function is e^(-Y)sum_(l=0)^(k-1)Y^l/l!. Exponential tilting changes
the first phase mean to1/2 and each of the q other phase means to
(k-1)/(q+k-1), with normalizing factor (1/2)(q/(q+k-1))^q.
The degree-l complete homogeneous polynomial for these means is exactly
the inner sum in (2), by expanding (1-z/2)^(-1)(1-cz)^(-q).

Evaluate (2) over the finite integer range2<=k<=floor((d+1)/2)
and also include the k1 value1/2. Their minima and margins are:

| d | minimum | minimum minus (7/6)gamma_d |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | 1/2 | 1/128 |
| 4 | 13/27 | 61/16875 |
| 5 | 243/512 | 2147/373248 |
| 6 | 1472/3125 | 439904/52521875 |
| 7 | 21875/46656 | 32753357/3057647616 |
| 8 | 384912/823543 | 1348942633648/106352477257509 |
| 9 | 15647317/33554432 | 939511987337/65536000000000 |

All entries follow from the finite sums of rational numbers in (2), and
all denominators and margin numerators are positive. There are only the
explicitly specified integer k values in this finite part. The root
computed every entry with exact rational arithmetic; the argument for
all unbounded dimensions is the preceding analytic gamma-tail bound.
This proves (1) in the full stated coefficient class.
